title: Olive Oil Focaccia
cScaleSummary: C0 because the recipe contains no animal-derived ingredients that contribute cholesterol. The flour, olive oil, yeast, rosemary, salt, and water all contribute 0 mg cholesterol.
ldlActiveSummary: LDL-Active is false because the recipe is primarily a refined-flour bread designed around texture and fermentation rather than a fiber-forward structure specifically intended to support LDL lowering.
intro: Focaccia is one of Italy’s great flatbreads: olive oil-rich, deeply dimpled, salty, and built around contrast. The best versions are not just soft bread. They have a crisp fried-bottom crust, a tender open crumb, and pockets of oil and brine that season the dough from the surface down. It is simple food, but the technique matters.

stepGroups.title: Mix the Dough
items: In a large bowl, combine the 500 g bread flour, 390 g water, 10 g fine sea salt, 4 g instant yeast, and 15 g extra-virgin olive oil. Mix until no dry flour remains. The dough will be sticky and loose.

stepGroups.title: Strengthen the Dough
items: With wet hands, stretch one side of the dough up and fold it over itself. Rotate the bowl and repeat on all four sides. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Repeat the stretch-and-fold process two more times, resting 20 minutes between each round. The dough should become smoother, more elastic, and slightly bubbly.
Cover the bowl and let the dough rise at room temperature for 2 to 3 hours, until noticeably expanded and airy.

stepGroups.title: Pan and Proof
items: Coat a half-sheet pan generously with 30 g olive oil. Scrape the dough into the pan and turn it once so both sides are lightly coated.
Gently stretch the dough toward the corners. Do not force it. If it resists, rest it for 15 minutes, then continue stretching.
Cover and let rise for 1½ to 2 hours, until puffy and nearly filling the pan.

stepGroups.title: Dimple and Bake
items: In a small bowl, stir together the 60 g water and 6 g fine sea salt until dissolved.
Drizzle the remaining 10 g olive oil over the dough. Pour the salt water evenly across the surface.
With oiled fingers, press deep dimples across the entire dough, pushing straight down to the pan without tearing. The brine and oil should pool in the dimples.
Scatter the chopped rosemary over the top and sprinkle with the flaky sea salt.
Bake for 22 to 28 minutes, until the top is golden and the bottom is deeply crisp.

stepGroups.title: Cool and Serve
items: Remove the focaccia from the pan and cool on a rack for at least 15 minutes before cutting.
